Lost and Found: Shadow School — The Final Escape

LOST & FOUND // SHADOW SCHOOL

Year 5 Reading & Writing adventure

Finish the mission, copy your final report, then submit it in the Google Form.

Controls: W/S move · A/D turn · SPACE fire · E interact · 1–5 equipment. Complete the case files, defeat the shadows, and write your report.

HOW TO PLAY

1. Start: Press START MISSION, then press CONTINUE / SKIP.

2. Move: Press W to walk forward. Press A or D to turn. Press S to move backward.

3. Read: Walk towards a glowing file and press E (or READ). Read the passage, choose an answer, and close the box.

4. Collect ammo: Read the question at a glowing ammo terminal. A correct answer gives ammunition. You can also select SKIP.

5. Clear shadows: Face a shadow and press SPACE (or FIRE). Collect green health pickups if your health drops.

6. Finish: Complete the three files, clear the four main shadows, write at least three sentences, then follow the cyan portal.

The mission list is on the left. After a while, it gives directions if you are lost. Secrets marked ? are optional.

PIXEL DETECTIVE // SHADOW SCHOOL

Soundtrack: Original synthesized retro-metal loop, not copyrighted DOOM audio. Toggle MUSIC ON to enable. Desktop: W/S move, A/D turn, Q/E strafe/read (E reads), SPACE fire at a nearby shadow, 1/2/3 choose equipment, and 4/5 use the secret boss weapons once unlocked. Touch: hold direction buttons and tap FIRE LASER or READ. Collect glowing ammo terminals and answer a question to unlock laser charges. Most shadows take 2–3 hits, but a precise headshot clears them instantly. Look for the secret ? marker, explore the hidden room, and after writing survive the final shadow wave and follow the cyan portal marker to finish. Optional bonus terminals and faded wall notes can be read with E. A hidden boss chamber may also open.

Teacher notes · DSKP and assessment

Year 5 Reading LS 3.2.2: understand specific information and details in texts of two paragraphs or more. Year 5 Writing LS 4.2.4: describe objects using suitable statements. The three case files each contain two paragraphs. Wall-mounted chains and other decorations are visual only and do not change the lesson objectives. The three extra bonus passages and two hidden notes are voluntary reading comprehension practice. Ammo terminals also require reading two paragraphs. The five reading questions measure retrieval of specific details; shadows are cleared with non-violent laser effects after earning ammunition through reading comprehension. Final writing requires at least three descriptive sentences and a self-checklist, followed by a spawned exit portal and branching cutscenes. Teacher assessment is required for the quality of original writing. The game is a component of a Google Sites resource, not a substitute for the full ASSURE plan, multimedia instruction, references or feedback collection.
